sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Apollo Techno Industries Limited; BSE SME; ISIN INE0X4A01013. Research cutoff 2026-10-20. Dated quote ₹90.51 on 2026-10-16, not a live executable bid. Five-year nominal INR scenarios use a 15% analyst equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative position. Current scope and capital bridge are described in financial forensics and the linked model.

Apollo Techno Industries, BSE 544671/ATIL, ISININE 0 X 4 A 01013, listed December 31 2025; not Gujarat Apollo or Apollo Micro Systems. October 19 master confirms 13.689 m shares and 1000-share lot. Consolidated analysis includes wholly owned Apollo Techno Equipments, acquired in 2021. FY 26 parent revenue 103.6258 plus subsidiary 24.4839 less internal 17.7287 equals 110.381 cr. [S1][P1][SEC]

Gate conclusions: G 1 Integrity: Repeated lender-data and RPT disclosure weaknesses; no established fraud finding. G 2 Reliability: Cash financing reclassification and tax-unit error reconciled; remaining asset-quality uncertainty explicitly stressed. G 3 Funding: Positive equity but heavy WC; new debt requirements modeled and not assumed approved. G 4 Tradability: Conditional secondary liquidity estimate only, pending live BSE implementation verification.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Specialized HDD/foundation rigs, service capability and product development offer differentiation but compete with domestic/imported equipment. Small machine volumes, cyclical contractors and customer concentration limit pricing power; not a broad recurring software-like revenue base. Finished goods 92.4091 cr, spares 17.3573 cr, services approximately 0.419 cr; prior trading 11.6225 cr disappears. Spare sales add aftermarket exposure but no contractual recurring-revenue claim. Warranty expense 0.1804 cr is already in operating costs. [S1][P1][NEW]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: ACE provides relevant Indian equipment/service and contractor-cycle context, but its broad crane, handling, agriculture and construction portfolio and much larger scale differ. FY 26 chairman reports 3395 cr total income,614 cr EBITDA and 425 cr PAT; these are not Apollo-comparable operating revenue/margins. No current ACE market multiple is copied into Apollo valuation. [PEER]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: FY 23–26 revenue 71.7255/68.9767/99.1409/110.381 cr gives approximately 15.45% CAGR, initial 7 adjusted down 1 for deceleration to 11.34% and machine-unit growth 47/60/61 versus price/product/export mix. No acquisition perimeter jump assumed; longstanding subsidiary is consolidated. Prospectus FY 23/24/25 PAT 0.8963/3.2306/13.7884 cr; latest annual comparative 13.7345 differs 0.0539 cr, not alone a critical error. Machine volumes and mix, not just CAGR, anchor assessment. [S1][P1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Operating NOPAT 9.9083 cr on average equity-plus-full-debt 80.3734 cr gives 12.33%; incremental operating NOPAT is negative as capital rises 46.849 cr. Late IPO cash depresses ratio but inventory/receivable funding also genuinely increases capital intensity. March inventory 51.5928 cr and conservative net operating WC 78.8931 cr dominate capital employed. Base cash-funded growth cannot assume WC ratios collapse; stress borrowing explicitly modeled. [S1]

Trenchless infrastructure and foundation work support runway; domestic soil-testing-rig launch July 16 extends range. Top 10 customers 58.03% and top 1 18.45% inFY 25, versus 67.01% top 10 inQ 1 FY 26, make demand lumpy. Capacity is product-mix-dependent, not a verified fixed-unit expansion promise. Track realized orders and collections from new rigs, not launch publicity. No verified FY 26 unit-volume or fixed aggregate capacity denominator found; model does not invent it. [P1][NEW]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter 73.05%; recurrent materially different current-asset submissions to lenders, missing external balance confirmations, and related land allocation subsequently reversed weaken controls. May recovery remedies 3 cr exposure; no fraud finding inferred. FZCO was related in prospectus but omitted from FY 26 RPT table without clear relationship bridge. CFO resigned August 31 for personal reasons; no adverse reason inferred. March 26 lender assets submitted 72.1579/65.7819 cr against books 61.2174 cr, differences 10.9405/4.5645 cr. Management cites timing/cancellation; recurrence and scale warrant more weight than minor drafting. Director/family pay 1.2388 cr versus 1.2258 cr. FZCO FY 25 related sales 18.2938 cr and receivable 9.7251 cr are not eliminated as subsidiary business; FY 26 omission cannot be taken as zero economic exposure. [S1][P1][CFO][BOARD]

June monitoring confirms 38.50 cr WC and 3.63 cr GCP deployed. Promoter-director land advance 3 cr under December 29 MOU cancelled as unsuitable; refund with interest 3.05 cr receivedMay 2 after March 29 cheque. Refund redeployed to salary/operations duringQ 1. Monitoring 0.11 cr GCP excess attributedTDS/issue-cost reallocation; not a material diversion conclusion. CFOAugust 31 resignation states personal reasons; board 2025 date is drafting inconsistency against dated resignation 2026, not evidence of concealed earlier exit. July 16 ST 300 launch verified; no replacement CFO filing located. [MON][MONMAR][CFO][BOARD][NEW]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Reported CFO−29.8295/+15.1776 cr includes financing ST-debt changes−1.8568/+1.0037 cr. Removing these yields−27.9727/+14.1739 cr. Prospectus FY 23/24/25 CFO−0.9683/2.8035/14.4607 uses restated classifications, so no falsely exact spliced four-year conversion. FY 26 cash capex 1.8837 cr is small relative to inventory 14.7956 and receivable 14.0089 cash absorption. IPO net 41.9826 cr funds the gap rather than proving cash earnings. [S1][P1]

Gross receivables 33.404 cr include 7.8409 cr aged 1–2 years,0.2248 cr 2–3 years and 0.5624 cr older; ECL 0.0562 cr. Aging uses posting date rather than contractual due date. Audit note says no debtor/creditor confirmations received by signing, while opinion remains unmodified. FY 23 supplier advance 0.8221939 cr to Millenium Link East lacked confirmation; subsequent refund undertaking supported removal of qualification, but final cash recovery not located. Model 5/15 cr loss cases are hypothetical portfolio stresses, not alleged writeoffs. [S1][P1][SUB25]

Annual consolidated note 54 prints VAT/CST 1,409 under lakhs, apparently 14.09 cr. Audited subsidiary FY 25 note 33 explicitly uses thousands 1,409, while prospectus 209 itemizes Rs 14,09,112. Supported gross amount is 0.1409112 cr, not 14.09 cr. Prior deposit 0.0646 cr requires current reconciliation. GST appeals 0.2707+0.3293+0.0843 cr add 0.6843 cr. Modelgross 0.8252112 cr immediate settlement is a downside sensitivity, not expected tax bill; unidentified tax assets excluded and separately recoverable sensitivity prevents invented setoff. Subsidiary 15.19 cr parent guarantee overlaps consolidated debt. [S1][P1][SUB25]

PAT 11.0442 cr falls from 13.7345 cr; operating EBIT 13.2111 cr versus 16.9145 cr also declines, so deferred-tax swing is not the whole explanation. Other income 2.169 cr includes 1.6425 cr FX. Current-share EPS 8.07 is below weighted 10.11. FY 26 tax expense 1.9947 cr comprises current 0.0489, prior−0.0277 and deferred 1.9735; prior deferred credit 2.4753 made historical profit flattering. Forecast uses 25% tax, excludes other income and exceptional items. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Base/bear/bull five-year IRRs 11.02%/-19.32%/32.73%; terminal prices 152.68/30.95/372.83 rupees. Base 15% hurdle entry 75.91. Five-/ten-times price at 18 x terminalPAT requires 34.42/68.83 crPAT versus 11.04 cr current, with additional WC funding. Not a supported multibagger promise. [S1][MARKET]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Equipment downturn and 10–15 cr asset losses can require new borrowing and impair equity; book equity is not cash recovery assurance. Severe model explicitly funds the gap rather than assigning a positive multiple to negative earnings.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-/ten-times price at 18 x terminalPAT requires 34.42/68.83 crPAT versus 11.04 cr current, with additional WC funding. Not a supported multibagger promise. [S1][MARKET]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Watchlist, not unqualified buy: specialist products and moderate headline P/E compete with weaker operating margin, concentrated export/group balances and expensive cash conversion. Thesis improves only with aged receivable recovery, stock turns, reconciled lender reports, FZCO relationship/current-balance disclosure and funded profitable orders. Escalate if cash conversion stays negative despite slower sales, additional promoter advances appear, or refinancing terms dilute minority economics. [S1][P1][MON]

sections.text:
Specialist drilling equipment has real product growth, but FY 26 operating profit fell and inventory/receivables consumed the IPO cash. A dramatic-looking VAT amount is resolved as a unit error, while lender-reporting discrepancies, aged/group exposures and thin executable liquidity remain substantive risks. IAS assumes the explicitly conservative secondary-liquidity case, not confirmed live tradability.

sections.text: Primary annual/prospectus filings, subsequent announcements, relevant operating peers and dated market sources are individually linked in the source ledger. Facts, calculations, management claims and assumptions are distinguished in the evidence audit. FY 26 FZCO relationship/current exposure not bridged despite prior related sales and balances. No independent receipt verification for aged debtors or Millenium supplier advance. No full current tax-deposit/type bridge; conservative non-recovery and gross-settlement sensitivities explicit. Secondary BSE prices/volume are not verified traded-value or live-depth data; five calendar gaps and surveillance status unresolved. Forecast debt is required, not an approved facility; financing failure requires slower growth or dilution.

These operating expenses are included in the full FY27 modeled margin and WC, not an additional cash windfall or a second3cr expense. Current cash balance after June deployment is not observed.

All4.5898cr unsplit statutory assets are excluded from opening operating WC. Gross contingent claims0.8252112cr are stressed as an immediate settlement deduction, not asserted expected loss; no related provision identified in current employee/expense provisions. FY26 operating EBIT13.2111cr excludes2.169cr other income and exceptional loss; base12% margin tracks that underlying level. Bull15% remains below prior17.06%; bear8% and severe3% stress operating leverage. No repeated FX gains or tax credits support forecast earnings.

Base12% growth approximates current11.34% and is below three-year15.45%; manufacturing/spares growth and July product launch support opportunity but not assured orders. Physical machine units47/60/61 throughFY25 limit extrapolation of price/mix.

Base70% net operating WC is close to71.47% conservative opening ratio; bull60% needs real collections, bear80% and severe95% stress stock/credit. Capex3% sales exceeds current1.7%; depreciation1.2%, interest10% on opening full debt,25% normalized tax. Required new debt is not an approved facility; unavailable credit implies slower growth or dilution.

Terminal10/14/18x operating NOPAT, severe8x, are explicit analyst sensitivities, not copied ACE multiples. All debt is subtracted; subsidiary guarantee15.19cr for parent borrowing is not added a second time. No dividends assumed.
